name: Craft Cottage
use: Closed (formerly the Marriage and Family Therapy clinic; earlier arts-and-crafts center, nursery school, Home Economics practice house)
builtText: before 1893; moved to Ballard Street in 1932
statusNote: Closed since about 2021, when the family therapy clinic left

renovations.what: Converted into a Marriage and Family Therapy clinic, which saved it from demolition

facts.text: Originally part of General Hoyt's property on Main Street; known around 1897 as 'The Orphanage' when rented as a bachelor residence.
Served as the Home Economics practice house from 1918 to 1930, then a nursery school.
Moved in 1932, next to the Elizabeth DeMeritt House, to clear the site for Scott Hall.
Was an arts-and-crafts center (hence 'Craft Cottage') until the 1980s; the MFT clinic closed about 2021 and the building is now closed.

verdict: A 19th-century clapboard house moved to Ballard Street in 1932, now closed and empty.
notes: Category 'administration' fits poorly: the building is closed, and its last use was a clinic (academic/CHHS). Old data's 'in use, small office cottage' is wrong per Clio. Clio says it stands on Ballard Street among Scott, Smith, Sawyer and Stillings. No licensed photo found anywhere; ref-01 (archives) shows a two-story clapboard house with bay windows.
judgeNotes: Archives photo only. Still ranked as a closed building.
